items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Zack and Johnny came to my house... asked me if I would like to be a part of the group... Johnny Johnson played nice piano... I didn't raise too much hell on trumpet.

ctx.x: We never had any job with Hershal which was a pity because I believe that we would have been more inspired playing for dancers than we were at the rehearsals which were quite inspiring with Hershal. Brown at the keyboard.

Sometime later a fellow came to Cincinnati from Kentucky who's name was Zack White. His name was really Zacharias White and he played banjo. There was also a pianist named Johnny Johnson that I had heard when I was living on Kenyon Avenue. Johnny Johnson also played piano by ear and he was well known in the higher society negro class.

One day Zack and Johnny came to my house and told me that there was a fellow in town from Michigan that wanted some musicians to play week-ends at a vacation camp not far from Kalamazoo, and they asked me if I would like to be a part of the group. I had never been more than a hundred miles from Cincinnati and this proposition sounded great to me. Zack and Johnny did not have to ask me twice if I wanted to go with them.
